views.name: hardware_sales_monthly_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  date AS date,
  product_code AS product_code,
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  COALESCE(sold_quantity,0) AS sold_quantity,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly

params.description: Monthly cleaned sales facts at the grain of (date, product_code, customer_code) answering how many units of a product were sold to a customer in a given month and the fiscal year for that month.
params.when_to_use: Get the per-month quantity sold for a specific product and customer (time series at month grain). | Join to product or customer dimensions to add descriptive attributes while preserving monthly, product, customer granularity. | Compute higher-level aggregates (by product-month, customer-month, product-year, customer-year) by aggregating sold_quantity from this view.
params.when_not_to_use: Use this view to answer per-order or per-transaction questions — it is monthly aggregated and does not contain order-level identifiers; joining to order-level tables will cause incorrect duplication. | Use this view as-is to compute counts of distinct orders, transactions, or events — sold_quantity is a numeric measure aggregated to month; counting rows here does not reflect underlying event counts. | Join this view to one-to-many tables (for example, multiple price rows, multiple deductions, or multiple web orders) without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply sold_quantity and produce over-counts. Always aggregate the one-to-many side to the same (date, product_code, customer_code) grain before joining or join only to one-row-per-key dimension tables.
params.output_schema: date: month/date value representing the period of the monthly sales row — derived from hardware_fact_sales_monthly.date | product_code: product identifier for the sold item — derived from hardware_fact_sales_monthly.product_code | customer_code: customer/account identifier for the purchase — derived from hardware_fact_sales_monthly.customer_code | sold_quantity: number of units sold for this product to this customer in this month. COALESCE(sold_quantity, 0) — source: hardware_fact_sales_monthly.sold_quantity | fiscal_year: fiscal year label for the month (as stored) — derived from hardware_fact_sales_monthly.fiscal_year
params.metric: sold_quantity = COALESCE(hardware_fact_sales_monthly.sold_quantity, 0)  -- numeric measure at grain (date, product_code, customer_code) | no other derived aggregates are defined in this view; higher-level metrics must be computed by aggregating sold_quantity across the view's grain (e.g., SUM(sold_quantity) GROUP BY date, product_code to get product-month totals).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to hardware_product_master on product_code — safe because hardware_product_master is a product dimension (one row per product_code), so joining will not duplicate sold_quantity. | cardinality-SAFE: join to hardware_customer_master on customer_code — safe because hardware_customer_master is a customer dimension (one row per customer_code), so joining will not duplicate sold_quantity. | cardinality-SAFE: join to accounts_with_rep_and_region on customer_code (or account key) if that view is one-row-per-customer — safe only if that sibling is truly one-row-per-customer_code; verify its grain before joining. | NOT SAFE: do NOT directly join to hardware_prices_by_year, hardware_costs_by_year, or hardware_customer_deductions_by_year if those tables contain multiple rows per (product_code, fiscal_year) or (customer_code, fiscal_year) without first aggregating or restricting to a single row, because multiple price/cost/deduction rows per year would multiply sold_quantity when joined. | NOT SAFE: do NOT join directly to web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date or any order-level or multi-row-per-(date,product_code,customer_code) table without ensuring that the other table is aggregated to (date,product_code,customer_code) (or to a coarser desired grain and then re-aggregating sold_quantity). Otherwise the one-to-many join will replicate rows and over-count sold_quantity. | NOT SAFE: do NOT join to the JOIN-type siblings (sales_monthly_enriched, accounts_with_rep_and_region, offerings_with_faculty, students_with_enrollment_and_gpa) without confirming their grain. For example, sales_monthly_enriched may already combine dimensions — joining both could be redundant or multiply measures. | When combining with a one-to-many sibling, instead: aggregate the one-to-many side to (date, product_code, customer_code) or aggregate this view to the coarser target grain before joining and then combine measures appropriately (e.g., join aggregated sums).
params.comparison: use sales_monthly_enriched instead when you need pre-joined descriptive attributes from product/customer/pricing in a single view — sales_monthly_enriched likely contains the same monthly sales rows but already joined to other dimensions. | use monthly_sales_by_product_year or monthly_sales_by_customer_year when you need pre-aggregated metrics at the product-year or customer-year grain — these sibling views have aggregated sold_quantity and are appropriate when you must avoid re-aggregation errors. | do not replace hardware_prices_by_year or hardware_costs_by_year with this view — those siblings provide price/cost time series per product-year (different grain and different measures).

views.description: Normalized/cleaned monthly hardware sales fact. Parses/normalizes the date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD (keeps as TEXT), ensures numeric sold_quantity and fiscal_year are preserved. Use this as the canonical monthly sales input to downstream joins/aggregations to avoid repeated casts or NULL surprises. | Use for: monthly sales trends for a product/customer/market; aggregate sold_quantity by year/quarter/month; join to price/cost/discount by fiscal_year

views.name: hardware_product_master
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  division AS division,
  segment AS segment,
  category AS category,
  product AS product,
  variant AS variant
FROM hardware_dim_product

params.description: A normalized product master keyed at product_code that provides canonical product attributes (division, segment, category, product, variant).
params.when_to_use: Look up product attributes (division, segment, category, product name, variant) for a given product_code. | Annotate sales, price, cost, or customer datasets at the product_code grain with stable descriptive attributes. | Build dimension joins in reporting or modeling where a single row per product_code is required.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to a fact table and then aggregating without ensuring the fact is the aggregation target — WHY: this view is 1 row per product_code (dimension); joining it to a fact is safe only if the fact is the aggregation target. Do not treat this view as an aggregated metric source. | Using this view to answer time-series or year-specific price/cost questions — WHY: it contains only static product attributes from hardware_dim_product, not time-varying measures such as prices or costs by year; use hardware_prices_by_year or hardware_costs_by_year instead. | Expecting it to deduplicate cases where hardware_dim_product has multiple rows per product_code — WHY: the SQL selects directly from hardware_dim_product assuming product_code is the grain; if the underlying table contains duplicates, this view will expose them and can silently multiply rows when joined. | Attempting to compute aggregates (counts, sums) of products across cohorts without first deciding the appropriate de-duplication — WHY: counting product_code here is only meaningful if hardware_dim_product is known to be unique on product_code; otherwise you must deduplicate or aggregate in a downstream step.
params.output_schema: product_code: canonical product identifier — derived directly from hardware_dim_product.product_code | division: product division attribute — derived directly from hardware_dim_product.division | segment: product segment attribute — derived directly from hardware_dim_product.segment | category: product category attribute — derived directly from hardware_dim_product.category | product: product name/description attribute — derived directly from hardware_dim_product.product | variant: product variant attribute — derived directly from hardware_dim_product.variant
params.grounded_columns: hardware_dim_product.product_code | hardware_dim_product.division | hardware_dim_product.segment | hardware_dim_product.category | hardware_dim_product.product | hardware_dim_product.variant
params.metric: No derived aggregates or expressions in this view; all outputs are direct column projections. | If you need a derived metric such as product_count, define it externally as COUNT(DISTINCT hardware_product_master.product_code) after verifying uniqueness of hardware_dim_product.product_code.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables (e.g., monthly_sales_by_product_year, hardware_sales_monthly_clean) on product_code — safe because hardware_product_master is expected to be one-row-per-product_code so it will not duplicate fact measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to other one-row-per-product_code dimension views (if present) on product_code — safe for enrichment as long as both are truly 1:1 on product_code. | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views such as monthly_sales_by_product_year (AGG) if that aggregation is not already at product_code grain for the same period — WHY: if the target view has multiple rows per product_code (for different months/years/cohorts), joining is fine only when you intend to repeat the product attributes per period; however, joining to a raw one-to-many table (e.g., a non-aggregated sales line-items table) will multiply rows and require re-aggregation on the fact columns to produce correct measures. | do NOT join to sibling JOIN views that themselves expand cardinality (e.g., sales_monthly_enriched) without understanding their grain — WHY: if the sibling join produces multiple rows per product_code (e.g., by month or account), combining without re-aggregation will lead to double-counting when summing measures from the fact side.
params.comparison: use hardware_prices_by_year instead when you need time-varying price information for products — it contains prices by year while hardware_product_master has only static attributes. | use hardware_costs_by_year instead when you need time-varying cost information — hardware_product_master does not include costs. | use hardware_sales_monthly_clean or monthly_sales_by_product_year when your goal is to analyze sales metrics by product over time — those are fact/aggregated views; hardware_product_master is only descriptive. | use hardware_customer_master when you need customer-level attributes — sibling is for customers while this view is for products.

views.description: Canonical product dimension pass-through. Use when analyses need product descriptive attributes (division, segment, category, product, variant) keyed by product_code. | Use for: product-level rollups (by division/segment/category); enrich sales with product attributes

views.name: hardware_customer_master
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  customer AS customer,
  platform AS platform,
  channel AS channel,
  market AS market,
  sub_zone AS sub_zone,
  region AS region
FROM hardware_dim_customer

params.description: Provides the canonical customer master lookup for hardware customers: one row per customer_code with stable attributes (name, platform, channel, market, sub_zone, region).
params.when_to_use: Look up demographic/attribute information for a given customer_code. | Join to sales or transactions when you need customer attributes at customer granularity (one row per customer). | Populate reports or dashboards that require customer-level labels (region, market, platform) without aggregating measures.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view directly to transactional-level tables (e.g., orders, sales lines) when you expect to preserve transaction-level grain — doing so is OK, but be aware this view is at customer grain; if you instead join to a table that is many-rows-per-customer you must not assume this view introduces additional aggregation. If you later aggregate, ensure you aggregate the transactional table first to avoid double-counting. | Using this view as a source of time-series / per-period metrics — it contains no dates or measures. Using it as if it provides periodized measures will be silently wrong (grain mismatch). | Treating any attribute here as a historical/time-versioned value. The view selects current attributes from hardware_dim_customer; if attributes change over time, this view does not contain temporal history and will give the current attribute for all past transactions unless joined on a time-aware dimension.
params.output_schema: customer_code: unique identifier for the customer at the customer grain; derived from hardware_dim_customer.customer_code | customer: human-readable customer name; derived from hardware_dim_customer.customer | platform: platform classification for the customer (e.g., web/retail/partner) ; derived from hardware_dim_customer.platform | channel: sales channel for the customer; derived from hardware_dim_customer.channel | market: market segmentation or country/market for the customer; derived from hardware_dim_customer.market | sub_zone: sub-region or smaller geographic partition; derived from hardware_dim_customer.sub_zone | region: higher-level geographic region for the customer; derived from hardware_dim_customer.region
params.grounded_columns: hardware_dim_customer.customer_code | hardware_dim_customer.customer | hardware_dim_customer.platform | hardware_dim_customer.channel | hardware_dim_customer.market | hardware_dim_customer.sub_zone | hardware_dim_customer.region
params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics in this view. All outputs are direct attribute selections (identity mappings) from hardware_dim_customer.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to transactional or aggregate tables ON customer_code — safe because this view is one-row-per-customer_code, so it will not duplicate measures when joined to tables that are many-rows-per-customer (the duplication comes from the other side, not this view). Example: JOIN monthly_sales_by_customer_year m ON hardware_customer_master.customer_code = m.customer_code — safe since monthly_sales_by_customer_year is already aggregated to customer/time. | cardinality-SAFE: join to other one-row-per-customer dimensions/views such as accounts_with_rep_and_region ON customer_code — safe because both sides are at customer grain. | NOT safe without care: do NOT join this view to one-to-many tables (e.g., raw sales lines, web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date BEFORE aggregation) and then SUM this view's columns as if they were measures. Because this view has no measures, the risk is semantic: joining a many-rows-per-customer transactional table will repeat the customer attributes across rows; if a downstream process deduplicates incorrectly or assumes uniqueness, results will be wrong. Instead, either (a) aggregate the transactional side first, or (b) join and then aggregate using proper grouping keys. | NOT safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join to monthly_sales_by_product_year or other product-level multiples on product_id without ensuring a single join key per customer (those are many-to-many between customers and products). Such joins will multiply rows and require re-aggregation on the correct grain (customer or customer x product) depending on the analysis.
params.comparison: use accounts_with_rep_and_region instead when you need account-level rep or active-salesperson attributes in addition to region — that sibling may contain sales-rep or account-manager enrichments not present in hardware_customer_master. | use hardware_sales_monthly_clean, monthly_sales_by_customer_year, or monthly_sales_by_product_year when you need sales measures or time-series/aggregated metrics — hardware_customer_master contains no measures or dates. | use hardware_product_master when you need product master attributes; hardware_customer_master is focused solely on customer attributes and contains no product-related columns. | use sales_monthly_enriched when you need pre-joined sales data that already combines customer attributes with monthly sales measures; that view may handle time-appropriate joins and deduplication which hardware_customer_master alone does not.

views.description: Canonical customer dimension pass-through. Use when analyses need customer descriptive attributes keyed by customer_code. | Use for: sales by market/platform/channel/region; customer-level aggregation and segmentation

views.name: hardware_prices_by_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  gross_price AS gross_price
FROM hardware_fact_gross_price

params.description: Year-level gross price for each hardware product (one row per product_code and fiscal_year).
params.when_to_use: Look up the gross list price recorded for a product in a specific fiscal year. | Join product-level attributes (from product master) to a product-year price for reporting or labeling. | Filter by fiscal_year and product_code to get the canonical gross_price for that product-year for downstream calculations.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view directly to tables that are one-to-many to product_code (for example monthly sales rows) when you expect aggregated sales to align — doing so without re-aggregation will duplicate gross_price across the many-side rows and overstate any measure that multiplies price by quantity. | Using this view as if it were a sales or transaction fact (e.g., summing gross_price across products without weighting) — gross_price is a price attribute per product-year, not a sales amount; summing it across products gives a meaningless total unless that is the explicit intent. | Treating gross_price as a pre-aggregated revenue metric to join to customer or order-level rows directly — joining to finer grain facts (orders, monthly sales) will replicate the price per matching row and produce mis-counts unless you first aggregate or use the price only as a lookup.
params.output_schema: product_code: product identifier for the hardware product — derived from hardware_fact_gross_price.product_code | fiscal_year: fiscal year the price applies to — derived from hardware_fact_gross_price.fiscal_year | gross_price: gross (list) price for the product in that fiscal year — derived from hardware_fact_gross_price.gross_price
params.metric: gross_price = hardware_fact_gross_price.gross_price (attribute / measure recorded at product_code x fiscal_year grain; not an aggregate computed in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hardware_product_master on product_code — safe because hardware_product_master is expected to be one-row-per-product_code, so this view's product-year rows will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hardware_costs_by_year on (product_code, fiscal_year) — safe if hardware_costs_by_year is one-row-per-product_code x fiscal_year (it shares the same grain), because measures remain aligned and are not duplicated. | do NOT join directly to monthly_sales_by_product_year without checking aggregation: monthly_sales_by_product_year aggregates monthly rows to product-year and is safe to join on (product_code, fiscal_year) only if it is indeed aggregated to that same grain; if you join to a monthly or transaction-level table (e.g., sales_monthly_enriched or web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date) without first aggregating those rows to product_code x fiscal_year, gross_price will be duplicated across the many rows and any computed totals that multiply by price will be inflated. | do NOT join to hardware_customer_master, web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date, or other customer/order-level tables on product_code without re-aggregating the one-to-many side to product-year first, because those tables are typically many rows per product and will multiply this view's rows. | If you need to compute revenue = gross_price * quantity from a sales table, first aggregate quantity to product_code x fiscal_year (or join this view as a lookup and then aggregate the revenue), rather than joining this product-year price to transactional rows and then summing gross_price * quantity without grouping by product-year.
params.comparison: use hardware_costs_by_year instead when you need cost metrics (COGS) rather than gross list price — costs are the economic counterpart and likely share the same grain (product_code, fiscal_year) but represent a different measure. | use monthly_sales_by_product_year when you need aggregated sales volumes or revenue at the product-year grain — that view contains sales aggregates and is appropriate for revenue calculations; hardware_prices_by_year only provides the unit price attribute. | use hardware_product_master when you need product attributes (name, category, etc.) regardless of year — product_master is product-level (no fiscal_year) and should be joined to this view when you need both static product attributes and the year-specific price. | do not substitute sales_monthly_enriched or web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date for this view — those are transaction/month/account-level and contain different grains and metrics (sales, orders), whereas this view is a product-year price lookup.

views.description: Canonical gross price per product per fiscal_year. Use when joining yearly price data to sales aggregated to fiscal year or otherwise aligning by year. | Use for: compute revenue using gross_price and sold quantities aggregated by year; price trend analysis by product

views.name: hardware_costs_by_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  cost_year AS cost_year,
  manufacturing_cost AS manufacturing_cost
FROM hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost

params.description: Yearly manufacturing cost per product (one row per product_code × cost_year).
params.when_to_use: Lookup the manufacturing_cost for a specific product in a specific year. | Join yearly product-level cost to product attributes (e.g., product master) without changing cost totals. | Build time-series or year-over-year cost analyses at the product granularity after appropriate aggregation.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining directly to transaction-level or monthly sales tables to compute totals without re-aggregation — this will double-count or multiply costs because those tables can be many rows per product/year (grain mismatch). | Using this view to answer per-order or per-customer cost questions — the view's grain is product_code × cost_year, not order or customer. | Summing manufacturing_cost across a dimension that is not at product_code × cost_year without confirming unique keys — may produce incorrect totals if the join introduces duplicates. | Treating manufacturing_cost as an aggregate to be further aggregated across non-disjoint years or products without explicit grouping — could produce mis-counts if the consumer expects a different grain (e.g., monthly).
params.output_schema: product_code: product identifier at product granularity — derived from hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost.product_code | cost_year: year (numeric or integer) representing the cost reporting year — derived from hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost.cost_year | manufacturing_cost: monetary/decimal manufacturing cost for the product in that cost_year — derived from hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost.manufacturing_cost
params.metric: manufacturing_cost = manufacturing_cost (base measure from hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost; not aggregated in this view — value is whatever the source stores at the product_code × cost_year grain)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hardware_product_master on product_code — safe because hardware_product_master is a one-row-per-product_code dimension, so joining will not duplicate manufacturing_cost rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hardware_prices_by_year on (product_code, cost_year) — safe if hardware_prices_by_year is one-row-per-product_code × cost_year; it will align year and product without duplication. | do NOT join directly to monthly_sales_by_product_year (AGG) or sales_monthly_enriched (JOIN) without care — if those sibling views aggregate to multiple rows per product_code × cost_year (e.g., monthly rows or customer splits), joining without re-aggregation can multiply this view's manufacturing_cost when rolling up. | do NOT join to one-to-many tables such as web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date or staffhours_events_with_sequence without first aggregating those tables to product_code × cost_year — otherwise measures will be multiplied and totals will be wrong. | If you need to combine manufacturing_cost with a lower-grain table (e.g., monthly sales), aggregate the lower-grain table up to product_code × cost_year (or disaggregate cost appropriately if you have a reliable allocation key) before joining.
params.comparison: use hardware_prices_by_year instead when you need price/price-related metrics by product and year — that sibling contains pricing measures rather than manufacturing cost. | use monthly_sales_by_product_year when your analysis is driven by sales volume aggregated to product × year — that sibling provides sales aggregates which you should align to this view's grain before combining. | use hardware_product_master when you need descriptive product attributes (name, category, etc.) — join hardware_product_master to this view to enrich costs while preserving cardinality since product master is one-to-one on product_code.

views.description: Canonical manufacturing cost per product per cost_year. Use when aligning manufacturing_cost to sales aggregated by year. | Use for: compute margin using manufacturing cost and revenue by year; cost trend analysis by product

views.name: hardware_customer_deductions_by_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  pre_invoice_discount_pct AS pre_invoice_discount_pct
FROM hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions

params.description: Provides, at the customer × fiscal year grain, the pre-invoice discount percentage recorded in the pre-invoice deductions fact.
params.when_to_use: Look up the pre-invoice discount percent for a specific customer in a specific fiscal year. | Join customer-level fiscal-year pricing/discount attributes (as a dimension) onto other aggregates when you need the discount percent as a lookup attribute. | Reporting or filtering when you need the recorded pre-invoice discount percent per customer-year (not an aggregated or averaged discount across invoices).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to compute total (weighted) discount amounts across invoices or to infer invoice-level or line-level discounts — this view exposes a percent value that lives at customer × fiscal_year grain; treating it as an invoice- or line-level measure will mis-count if there are multiple invoices/lines per customer-year. | Do not aggregate this view (e.g., AVG(pre_invoice_discount_pct)) and assume it equals an invoice-weighted discount rate. Averaging customer-year percentages without weighting by invoice/base amounts yields incorrect business metrics (aggregation/grain mismatch). | Do not join this view directly to one-to-many transactional tables (e.g., invoice lines, orders) without re-aggregating or enforcing a join key that preserves the one-row-per-customer-year cardinality — otherwise the discount percent will be duplicated across many rows and inflate downstream results. | Do not use this view to answer questions about discounts by product, month, or rep unless you first align grains (re-aggregate by customer-product-year or customer-month) because the source grain is strictly customer × fiscal_year.
params.output_schema: customer_code: The customer identifier (sourced from hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions.customer_code). This is the customer key at the view grain. | fiscal_year: The fiscal year (sourced from hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions.fiscal_year). This is the year key at the view grain. | pre_invoice_discount_pct: The pre-invoice discount percentage (sourced from hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions.pre_invoice_discount_pct). This is a recorded percent value associated with the customer × fiscal_year in the source fact.
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE: join to hardware_customer_master on customer_code — safe because hardware_customer_master is a one-row-per-customer dimension, so joining will not duplicate this view's rows or its discount values. | Cardinality-SAFE: join to hardware_prices_by_year on (customer_code, fiscal_year) only if hardware_prices_by_year is one-row-per-(customer,fiscal_year); verify that sibling view's grain matches before joining to avoid accidental duplication. | Do NOT join directly to monthly_sales_by_product_year, monthly_sales_by_customer_year, web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date, or any transactional/aggregated-by-month/product view that is one-to-many to customer-year without re-aggregation — joining to those will multiply the pre_invoice_discount_pct value across many rows and produce incorrectly weighted results. | If you must combine with lower-grain data (e.g., invoices, order lines, monthly sales), either: (a) aggregate the lower-grain table up to customer_code × fiscal_year (e.g., SUM(amount) GROUP BY customer_code, fiscal_year) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate measures in a way that accounts for the duplication (e.g., compute weighted averages using invoice amounts as weights).
params.comparison: use hardware_customer_master instead when you need broader customer attributes (name, region, rep) — hardware_customer_master is a customer dimension and may include stable attributes not present in this fact-table-driven view. | use hardware_prices_by_year instead when you need price-specific annual metrics per product/customer-year (this view only exposes a discount percent; prices_by_year may include price, list price, or other pricing measures). | use monthly_sales_by_customer_year when you need sales aggregates at customer × year derived from monthly transactional data — that view contains aggregated sales amounts; this discount view only supplies a percent attribute and is not an aggregate of sales. | use sales_monthly_enriched or web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date when you need invoice/order-level or monthly transactional context — those sibling views provide transactional granularity, whereas this view is a lookup at customer × fiscal_year.

views.description: Canonical pre-invoice deduction percentage per customer per fiscal_year. Use to apply discounts when aggregating sales to year/customer. | Use for: apply customer discounts to yearly revenue calculations; analyze discount rates by customer and year

views.name: sales_monthly_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.date AS date,
  s.product_code AS product_code,
  s.customer_code AS customer_code,
  s.sold_quantity AS sold_quantity,
  s.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  p.division AS division,
  p.segment AS segment,
  p.category AS category,
  p.product AS product,
  p.variant AS variant,
  c.customer AS customer,
  c.platform AS platform,
  c.channel AS channel,
  c.market AS market,
  c.sub_zone AS sub_zone,
  c.region AS region
FROM hardware_sales_monthly_clean AS s
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_product AS p ON s.product_code = p.product_code
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_customer AS c ON s.customer_code = c.customer_code

params.description: Enriched monthly sales at the grain of (date, product_code, customer_code) combining cleaned sales facts with product and customer master attributes.
params.when_to_use: Answering questions about how many units were sold (sold_quantity) in a specific month (date) for a specific product_code and customer_code, while also needing product and customer descriptive attributes (division, segment, category, product, variant, customer name, platform, channel, market, sub_zone, region). | Filtering or aggregating sales by product hierarchy (division/segment/category/product/variant) or customer geography/segmentation (platform/channel/market/sub_zone/region) while starting from the raw monthly sales transaction row-level grain. | Joining downstream to other one-row-per-entity dimension tables (for enrichment) without changing sold_quantity, or to aggregate this view to produce monthly totals by product, customer, region, etc.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to answer questions that require pre-aggregated measures across different grains (for example: monthly sales totals per product or per customer) expecting pre-computed aggregates — use the aggregate sibling views (monthly_sales_by_product_year or monthly_sales_by_customer_year) instead. Why: this view is at row-level (date, product_code, customer_code) and may contain multiple rows that need aggregation; using it as if it were already aggregated can lead to double-counting if you join then aggregate incorrectly. | Do not join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from (date, product_code, customer_code) without re-aggregating the many-side first. Why: joining to one-to-many detail (for example a line-item-level promotions table or multiple price records per product/date) will multiply sold_quantity and silently inflate measures. | Do not use this view to compute revenue or price-based metrics unless you explicitly join to the authoritative price/cost tables (hardware_prices_by_year, hardware_costs_by_year) and define the join keys and temporal logic. views.name: monthly_sales_by_product_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_sold_quantity
FROM hardware_sales_monthly_clean
GROUP BY product_code, fiscal_year

params.description: Monthly-aggregated sales rolled up to product × fiscal year: total sold quantity of each product in a fiscal year.
params.when_to_use: Report total units sold per product for an entire fiscal year (e.g., top-selling products by units in FY2024). | Join to product-level dimensions (product name, category) when you need yearly product totals. | Calculate year-over-year unit-change per product when the input metric is yearly totals.
params.when_not_to_use: When you need month-level or order-level detail — this view is aggregated to product × fiscal_year, so using it to examine months or to count orders will lose detail. | When you need revenue, gross margin, price, cost, or customer-level breakdowns — this view only contains sold quantity, not monetary amounts. | Joining this view to a table with multiple rows per product_per_year (e.g., monthly rows, order lines, or customer-level rows) without re-aggregation will multiply total_sold_quantity and produce inflated totals (grain-mismatch). | Using it as if it were additive across a different grain (for example summing total_sold_quantity across products to infer account-level sales) without ensuring product-to-account mapping is one-to-one will give incorrect results.
params.output_schema: product_code: product identifier; derived directly from hardware_sales_monthly_clean.product_code (group key). | fiscal_year: fiscal year identifier; derived directly from hardware_sales_monthly_clean.fiscal_year (group key). | total_sold_quantity: total units sold for that product in that fiscal year; derived as SUM(hardware_sales_monthly_clean.sold_quantity).
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hardware_product_master on product_code — safe because hardware_product_master is expected to be one row per product_code, so joining will not duplicate total_sold_quantity. | Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_ranked_by_year_sales on (product_code, fiscal_year) — safe when that sibling is one-row-per-product-per-year (it is a RANK view built on similar aggregation), so measures are not duplicated. | Do NOT join directly to hardware_sales_monthly_clean (or any other monthly/order-level table) without re-aggregating that table to product_code × fiscal_year first — those tables are many-rows-per-product-per-year and would multiply total_sold_quantity. | Do NOT join to customer-level or order-line level views (e.g., hardware_customer_master joins or web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date) that are many-to-one or many-to-many relative to product_code × fiscal_year without aggregating or deduplicating first; otherwise totals will be inflated. | If you need to combine this view with another aggregated view that has a coarser grain (for example monthly or customer-year aggregates), align grains by either (a) aggregating the finer-grained dataset to product_code × fiscal_year or (b) breaking this view down to the coarser grain if source detail is available; mixing unmatched grains is unsafe.
params.comparison: Use hardware_sales_monthly_clean when you need month-level or raw transactional rows (it is the normalized monthly source used to compute these yearly totals). | Use sales_monthly_enriched when you need enriched row-level context (e.g., joined dimensions or flags) before aggregation — that view preserves row-level detail and enrichments. | Use monthly_sales_by_customer_year when you need sales aggregated by customer × fiscal year (different grain: product vs customer). | Use products_ranked_by_year_sales when you need a pre-computed ranking of products by year (same product × fiscal_year grain but includes ranking metadata).

views.description: Aggregated sold_quantity per product per fiscal_year. One row per product_code x fiscal_year. Use when joining to yearly price/cost/deduction facts to compute revenue/margin. | Use for: yearly revenue = total_sold_quantity * gross_price; compare sales volume by product across years

views.name: monthly_sales_by_customer_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code AS customer_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_sold_quantity
FROM hardware_sales_monthly_clean
GROUP BY customer_code, fiscal_year

params.description: Monthly-aggregated sales totals rolled up to customer by fiscal year (total sold quantity per customer per fiscal year).
params.when_to_use: Report total quantity sold to each customer for a given fiscal year (e.g., rank customers by annual quantity). | Join annual customer-level sold quantities to customer attributes (region, account owner) without altering the quantity totals. | Trend or compare customers across fiscal years at the customer-year grain.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view directly to a product-level table (or any one-to-many detail) to compute product-level metrics — doing so will duplicate total_sold_quantity unless you re-aggregate at the appropriate grain. | Using it to get monthly or transaction-level numbers — the view is aggregated to customer + fiscal_year; it cannot answer month or sale-level questions. | Using it as a numerator or denominator in cohort calculations that require first purchase date or cohort by month without ensuring cohorts are computed at the same grain — mixing grains will produce silently incorrect cohort sizes. | Joining to tables that expand customer rows (e.g., multiple addresses per customer) without first reducing those tables to one row per customer will multiply totals (mis-count).
params.output_schema: customer_code: customer identifier — sourced from hardware_sales_monthly_clean.customer_code | fiscal_year: fiscal year of the sale — sourced from hardware_sales_monthly_clean.fiscal_year | total_sold_quantity: sum of sold_quantity for the customer in that fiscal_year — derived from SUM(hardware_sales_monthly_clean.sold_quantity)
params.composition: Safe to join to hardware_customer_master on customer_code — hardware_customer_master is expected to be one row per customer (or must be pre-aggregated to one row); joining will not duplicate total_sold_quantity because keys are one-to-one (customer_code). | Safe to join to accounts_with_rep_and_region on customer_code — that view is intended to provide one row per account/customer; it will not duplicate measures if it is one-row-per-customer. | Safe to join to hardware_prices_by_year or hardware_costs_by_year on (fiscal_year, product_key) only if those are pre-aggregated to customer-year or if you do NOT multiply by product-level prices; otherwise you must re-aggregate after the join. In other words: do NOT join this view directly to a product-year table on fiscal_year alone when that table contains multiple product rows per customer-year without re-aggregation. | Do NOT join to sales_monthly_enriched (which likely contains monthly or product-level rows) without re-aggregating sales_monthly_enriched to customer_code + fiscal_year. Directly joining would join each customer-year aggregated row to multiple monthly/product rows and thus multiply total_sold_quantity. | Do NOT join to monthly_sales_by_product_year or products_ranked_by_year_sales expecting to keep totals unchanged — those sibling views are aggregated at product-year and will duplicate rows unless you aggregate to customer-year first or join on mutually unique keys that preserve cardinality. | If you must combine with a one-to-many dimension (for example multiple addresses, deductions rows, or line-level orders), either (a) pre-aggregate that dimension to customer_code + fiscal_year (one row per customer-year), or (b) join and then re-aggregate SUM(total_sold_quantity) appropriately, but be aware re-aggregating SUM(total_sold_quantity) after a join is not meaningful unless the joined rows are independent metrics; prefer bringing metrics from detail tables and recomputing at the desired grain.
params.comparison: Use hardware_sales_monthly_clean when you need month-level or transaction-level detail (this AGG loses month/transaction granularity). | Use monthly_sales_by_product_year when you need totals broken down by product and year instead of by customer and year. | Use sales_monthly_enriched when you need pre-joined dimensions (product/customer attributes) at the monthly or line-level before aggregating to a custom grain. | Use hardware_customer_master when you need customer attributes (name, segment) — join that master to this view to enrich annual customer totals. | Use hardware_prices_by_year or hardware_costs_by_year when you need price/cost information by year for calculations — but join carefully as noted in composition to avoid duplicating quantities.

views.name: products_ranked_by_year_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_code,
  fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  total_sold_quantity AS total_sold_quantity,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fiscal_year ORDER BY total_sold_quantity DESC) AS sales_rank
FROM monthly_sales_by_product_year

params.description: Ranks products within each fiscal year by the total sold quantity that year.
params.when_to_use: Answer: "Which products sold the most units in a given fiscal year?" — list top products by quantity for a specific fiscal_year. | Provide year-by-year leaderboards of product sales quantity (e.g., top-N products by units sold per fiscal year). | Reporting or dashboards that need a stable per-product-per-year rank based on yearly sold quantity.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to monthly-level tables and then summing/aggregating again — WHY: the view is already at product_code × fiscal_year grain; joining to monthly data without re-aggregating will produce duplicate/over-counted quantities. | Using its sales_rank as a time-series rank across months — WHY: rank is computed partitioned by fiscal_year only, so it is not comparable at a monthly grain. | Treating sales_rank as a continuous metric to average or sum — WHY: ranks are ordinal labels and must not be aggregated arithmetically (e.g., averaging ranks across years is meaningless). | Using this view to answer customer-level questions (e.g., which customers bought most of a product) — WHY: it has no customer granularity and will mislead if used to infer customer behavior. | Assuming sales_rank is deterministic across ties without tie-handling awareness — WHY: the SQL uses RANK(), which gives tied rows the same rank and will skip subsequent ranks (e.g., ranks 1,1,3). If you need dense ranks or tie-breakers, use a different function/view.
params.output_schema: product_code: product identifier for the SKU/part — derived directly from monthly_sales_by_product_year.product_code | fiscal_year: fiscal year for the aggregated measures — derived directly from monthly_sales_by_product_year.fiscal_year | total_sold_quantity: total units sold for that product in that fiscal_year — derived directly from monthly_sales_by_product_year.total_sold_quantity | sales_rank: rank of the product within the fiscal_year ordered by total_sold_quantity desc — computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fiscal_year ORDER BY total_sold_quantity DESC) in this view
params.metric: total_sold_quantity = monthly aggregation precomputed in monthly_sales_by_product_year (see that view for its aggregation definition: sum of sold_quantity across months per product_code × fiscal_year) | sales_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fiscal_year ORDER BY total_sold_quantity DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to hardware_product_master on product_code — safe because hardware_product_master is expected to be one-row-per-product_code (dimension), so this view's per-product-year rows are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE: join to hardware_prices_by_year on (product_code, fiscal_year) — safe if hardware_prices_by_year is one-row-per-product_code × fiscal_year; joining preserves one row per product-year and does not multiply total_sold_quantity. | DO NOT join directly to sales_monthly_enriched or monthly-level tables (e.g., any monthly sales table) without re-aggregation — those are many-month rows per product and will multiply total_sold_quantity unless you aggregate back to product_code × fiscal_year first. | DO NOT join to one-to-many tables like hardware_customer_master (if used as customer-level multi-row per product) or web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date without careful aggregation — such joins will duplicate this view's measures. If you need customer- or order-level detail, start from the base monthly or order-level aggregates and re-aggregate to the intended grain. | If you join to monthly_sales_by_product_year itself (self-join), ensure join keys include fiscal_year and product_code to avoid row multiplication; self-joins on product_code only across years will create unintended cross-year duplicates.
params.comparison: use monthly_sales_by_product_year when you need the underlying aggregated measure (total_sold_quantity) or want to compute alternative ranks/partitions — it provides the base product_code × fiscal_year metrics before applying window ranking. | use sales_monthly_enriched when you need monthly-level context, order-level details, or to compute rolling-month metrics — it has finer time grain (monthly or order-level) appropriate for temporal analysis. | use hardware_product_master when you need descriptive product attributes (name, category) alongside product-year ranks — this view provides only codes and measures and must be joined to the master for descriptive fields. | use a custom ranking view if you require different tie behavior (e.g., DENSE_RANK) or additional partitioning (e.g., partition by product_category and fiscal_year) — this view uses RANK() partitioned only by fiscal_year.

views.description: Per-year ranking of products by total sold quantity. One row per product_code x fiscal_year with a rank column (higher volume = rank 1). Useful as a building block for Top-K product queries by year. | Use for: Top N products by year (downstream filter WHERE sales_rank <= N); identify rank/position changes across years

views.name: accounts_with_rep_and_region
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.name AS name,
  a.website AS website,
  a.lat AS lat,
  a.long AS long,
  a.primary_poc AS primary_poc,
  a.sales_rep_id AS sales_rep_id,
  r.name AS region_name,
  s.name AS sales_rep_name,
  s.region_id AS sales_rep_region_id
FROM web_accounts AS a
LEFT JOIN web_sales_reps AS s ON a.sales_rep_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN web_region AS r ON s.region_id = r.id

params.description: A person-level (account) view that returns each web account and its linked primary sales rep and that rep's region.
params.when_to_use: Look up account attributes alongside the assigned sales rep and that rep's region for display, export, or row-level filtering. | Join account-level events (orders, activities) to account attributes and sales rep metadata when you need one row per account. | Create lists, badges, or contact sheets that require account name, location, primary point-of-contact, and the assigned rep and region.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view directly to transactional/line-item tables expecting aggregated sums per account without re-aggregation — because this view is at account grain (one row per web_accounts.id) and does not perform aggregation; joining to many-row transaction tables is fine only when the transaction side is the many side and you aggregate transactions afterwards. | Using this view to answer time-series or monthly sales questions (e.g., 'sales this month by account') — it contains no date or sales metrics and will produce misleading results if assumed to include measures. | Assuming sales_rep fields represent a stable history: this view reflects the current relational keys in web_accounts -> web_sales_reps -> web_region; it does not capture historical assignments or changes over time. | Joining to other one-to-many tables (e.g., orders, events) without aggregating those tables first or otherwise deduplicating — doing so can inflate result counts or cause multiplicative duplicates when you expect one row per account.
params.output_schema: id: Account identifier — derived from web_accounts.id (base table alias a.id). This is the grain of the view (one row per id). | name: Account name — derived from web_accounts.name (a.name). | website: Account website URL — derived from web_accounts.website (a.website). | lat: Account latitude — derived from web_accounts.lat (a.lat). | long: Account longitude — derived from web_accounts.long (a.long). | primary_poc: Primary point-of-contact for the account — derived from web_accounts.primary_poc (a.primary_poc). | sales_rep_id: The assigned sales rep id for the account — derived from web_accounts.sales_rep_id (a.sales_rep_id). Note: may be NULL if no rep assigned. | region_name: Name of the region of the account's sales rep — derived from web_region.name (r.name) via web_sales_reps.region_id. NULL if no rep or no matching region. | sales_rep_name: Name of the sales rep assigned to the account — derived from web_sales_reps.name (s.name). NULL if no rep assigned. | sales_rep_region_id: Region id of the sales rep — derived from web_sales_reps.region_id (s.region_id). NULL if no rep assigned.
params.grounded_columns: web_accounts.id | web_accounts.name | web_accounts.website | web_accounts.lat | web_accounts.long | web_accounts.primary_poc | web_accounts.sales_rep_id | web_sales_reps.id | web_sales_reps.name | web_sales_reps.region_id | web_region.id | web_region.name
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All output columns are direct column projections (1:1 mappings) from base tables; therefore derived_col = <no aggregate>
params.composition: Safe to join to dimensions that are 1:1 with account (this view's grain) — e.g., join to an account-level enrichment view on accounts.id because both sides are one row per account and will not duplicate rows. | Safe to join to web_sales_reps by sales_rep_id (already done internally) because web_sales_reps.id is a primary key (one row per rep) and the LEFT JOIN preserves one row per account — it does not duplicate account rows. | Safe to join to web_region by region id (already done internally via rep) because web_region.id is a primary key (one row per region) — this preserves cardinality. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables (for example web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date without pre-aggregation) unless the other side is aggregated to the account grain first. Example anti-pattern: accounts_with_rep_and_region JOIN web_orders ON accounts.id = web_orders.account_id will multiply account rows by each order row and can mis-count or require DISTINCT/aggregation to restore account-level results. | If you need to combine account attributes with per-account aggregated measures (orders, monthly sales), join to already-aggregated views (e.g., web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date aggregated to account) or perform an aggregation on the transactional side grouped by account.id before joining to avoid row multiplication and mis-counts.
params.comparison: use sales_monthly_enriched instead when you need account-level monthly sales or enriched transactional context — sales_monthly_enriched contains transactional/time information that this view lacks. | use web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date (or another aggregated orders view) instead when you want account-level sales metrics — accounts_with_rep_and_region provides only account and rep metadata and no sales metrics. | use students_with_enrollment_and_gpa or offerings_with_faculty when working in the academic domain — those sibling views join domain-specific entities (students, offerings) and are not substitutes for account/sales rep data. | There is no sibling view that returns the same account+rep+region columns with a different grain in the provided list; prefer this view when you explicitly want the one-row-per-web_accounts.id grain. If you need normalized rep or region tables separately, query web_sales_reps or web_region directly.

views.name: web_orders_aggregated_by_account_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  account_id AS account_id,
  SUBSTR(occurred_at,1,10) AS occurred_date,
  SUM(COALESCE(standard_qty,0)) AS total_standard_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(gloss_qty,0)) AS total_gloss_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(poster_qty,0)) AS total_poster_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(total,0)) AS total_qty,
  SUM(COALESCE(standard_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_standard_amt_usd,
  SUM(COALESCE(gloss_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_gloss_amt_usd,
  SUM(COALESCE(poster_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_poster_amt_usd,
  SUM(COALESCE(total_amt_usd,0.0)) AS total_amt_usd
FROM web_orders
GROUP BY account_id, SUBSTR(occurred_at,1,10)

params.description: Daily per-account aggregated counts and USD amounts of web orders, broken out by product type (standard, gloss, poster) and totals.
params.when_to_use: Report daily order volumes or revenue per account (e.g., "How many items and USD sold per account on 2026-07-01?"). | Feeding account-date level time-series dashboards, trend lines or churn analyses that require per-account-per-day metrics. | Joining to account-level dimensions (one row per account) to add metadata (region, rep) without changing numeric totals.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining directly to line-item or product-level tables (one-to-many to web_orders) and then summing — this will double-count because this view is already aggregated by account_id and date. | Using as a customer- or product-cohort source when the intended cohort grain is different (e.g., first-order date per account). This view is pre-aggregated by occurred_date and does not contain first-order flags or per-order identifiers. | Expecting order-level detail (order id, order line id, timestamps beyond date). This view collapses occurred_at to date via SUBSTR and loses ordering-level uniqueness. | Composing further aggregations without re-checking grain. Aggregating this view across additional dimensions that are more granular than account_id or occurred_date (for example, product_id or order_id) is invalid — you'll be aggregating an already-coarser grain and can't recover the missing detail.

views.name: staffhours_events_with_sequence
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  StaffMember AS StaffMember,
  EventDate AS EventDate,
  EventTime AS EventTime,
  EventType AS EventType,
  LAG(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS prev_event_type,
  LAG(EventDate) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS prev_event_date,
  LAG(EventTime) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS prev_event_time,
  LEAD(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS next_event_type,
  LEAD(EventDate) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS next_event_date,
  LEAD(EventTime) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime) AS next_event_time
FROM StaffHours

params.description: Row-level event sequence for each staff member: this view returns each StaffMember event at a specific EventDate and EventTime together with the immediately previous and next event (type, date, time) for that same staff member.
params.when_to_use: Investigating event-to-event transitions per staff member (e.g., what event preceded or followed a given event). | Calculating dwell times or durations between consecutive events for the same StaffMember (derive duration using EventDate/EventTime and prev/next fields). | Reconstructing ordered workflows or validating chronological ordering of StaffHours events per staff member.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to a higher-grain table containing multiple rows per StaffMember per EventDate/EventTime (e.g., detailed transactions) without re-aggregating — doing so can multiply rows and produce duplicated sequence context. | Using it as a pre-aggregated summary for counts or sums (e.g., total hours per day) — this view is row-level (one row per StaffMember+EventDate+EventTime) and not aggregated; aggregating after joining other tables may double-count if joins are many-to-one. | Assuming prev/next fields represent event adjacency across staff members — prev/next are partitioned by StaffMember only, so they intentionally do NOT cross staff boundaries; joining across staff members to compute cohort-level transitions without re-partitioning will be wrong. | Treating prev/next events as durable FK references to distinct event IDs — this view exposes the prior/next value at the same grain, but does not provide stable surrogate IDs; if you need immutable event identifiers, use the base StaffHours primary key (if present) instead.
params.output_schema: StaffMember: identifier for the staff member associated with this event — derived directly from StaffHours.StaffMember. | EventDate: date of the event (calendar date) — derived directly from StaffHours.EventDate. | EventTime: time (or timestamp) of the event — derived directly from StaffHours.EventTime. | EventType: categorical type of the current event (e.g., 'start','stop') — derived directly from StaffHours.EventType. | prev_event_type: EventType of the immediately prior event for the same StaffMember ordered by EventDate, EventTime — derived via LAG(EventType) over PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime on StaffHours.EventType. | prev_event_date: EventDate of the immediately prior event for the same StaffMember ordered by EventDate, EventTime — derived via LAG(EventDate) over PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime on StaffHours.EventDate. | prev_event_time: EventTime of the immediately prior event for the same StaffMember ordered by EventDate, EventTime — derived via LAG(EventTime) over PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime on StaffHours.EventTime. | next_event_type: EventType of the immediately next event for the same StaffMember ordered by EventDate, EventTime — derived via LEAD(EventType) over PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime on StaffHours.EventType. | next_event_date: EventDate of the immediately next event for the same StaffMember ordered by EventDate, EventTime — derived via LEAD(EventDate) over PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime on StaffHours.EventDate. | next_event_time: EventTime of the immediately next event for the same StaffMember ordered by EventDate, EventTime — derived via LEAD(EventTime) over PARTITION BY StaffMember ORDER BY EventDate, EventTime on StaffHours.EventTime.
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this view. The derived columns are window expressions that return neighboring row values: prev_event_type = LAG(StaffHours.EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffHours.StaffMember ORDER BY StaffHours.EventDate, StaffHours.EventTime) | prev_event_date = LAG(StaffHours.EventDate) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffHours.StaffMember ORDER BY StaffHours.EventDate, StaffHours.EventTime) | prev_event_time = LAG(StaffHours.EventTime) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffHours.StaffMember ORDER BY StaffHours.EventDate, StaffHours.EventTime) | next_event_type = LEAD(StaffHours.EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffHours.StaffMember ORDER BY StaffHours.EventDate, StaffHours.EventTime) | next_event_date = LEAD(StaffHours.EventDate) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffHours.StaffMember ORDER BY StaffHours.EventDate, StaffHours.EventTime) | next_event_time = LEAD(StaffHours.EventTime) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffHours.StaffMember ORDER BY StaffHours.EventDate, StaffHours.EventTime)
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE: join to one-row-per-staff reference/dimension tables on StaffMember (for example, a hypothetical staff_master view keyed by StaffMember) — safe because this view is one row per StaffMember+EventDate+EventTime and joining to a 1:1 staff dimension does not duplicate rows or the implicit sequence context. | Do NOT join directly to a table/view that is many-to-one from this view's grain (e.g., a table with multiple records per same StaffMember+EventDate+EventTime) without first aggregating that table to the same grain or using DISTINCT on keys — such joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate/alter sequence context (prev/next refer to rows in this view; duplicating rows will incorrectly imply multiple identical events). | Do NOT join to raw transactional tables keyed at a coarser or different grain (for example, per-day summaries or per-order rows) expecting this view's prev/next to remain valid; if you need aggregated measures (counts/sums) after joining, re-aggregate at the desired target grain to avoid mis-counting. | If you need to enrich with additional event attributes from StaffHours that are not present here, prefer joining back to a deduplicated StaffHours projection on (StaffMember, EventDate, EventTime) to avoid accidental multiplicative joins. | When computing derived durations (e.g., EventTime - prev_event_time), perform calculations within this view or in a query that preserves row-uniqueness by grouping on StaffMember+EventDate+EventTime before any many-to-one joins.
params.comparison: use students_with_enrollment_and_gpa when you need student-level enrollment and GPA context — that sibling is for a different domain and grain (students) and contains enrollment aggregates rather than per-event sequencing. | use offerings_with_faculty when you need course/offering-level joins to faculty — that view is focused on offerings and faculty relationships, not per-staff event sequencing. | use accounts_with_rep_and_region when you need stable one-row-per-account mapping to reps and regions — prefer it for 1:1 account enrichment instead of joining this event sequence directly to multi-row account activity tables. | No sibling view in the same DB provides the same per-StaffMember per-event sequencing; prefer this view when you specifically need immediate-prev/next event context, and prefer AGG sibling views (e.g., monthly_sales_by_product_year) only when you need aggregated metrics rather than row-level sequences.

One row per original event; includes lead/lag to compute durations between Enter/Exit pairs. | Use for: compute staff time-on-site between Enter and Exit; detect missing Enter/Exit pairs or anomalies in event sequences

views.name: students_with_enrollment_and_gpa
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.OfferNo AS OfferNo,
  e.StdNo AS StdNo,
  e.EnrGrade AS EnrGrade,
  s.StdFirstName AS StdFirstName,
  s.StdLastName AS StdLastName,
  s.StdCity AS StdCity,
  s.StdState AS StdState,
  s.StdZip AS StdZip,
  s.StdMajor AS StdMajor,
  s.StdClass AS StdClass,
  s.StdGPA AS StdGPA
FROM university_enrollment AS e
LEFT JOIN university_student AS s ON e.StdNo = s.StdNo

params.description: Provides one row per student enrollment (OfferNo, StdNo) combining enrollment attributes with the student's demographic and GPA attributes.
params.when_to_use: To list enrollments (offerings) and include the enrolled student's name, location, major, class, and GPA for reporting or downstream joins. | To display or export enrollment-level records that require student attributes without changing enrollment-level granularity. | To filter or count enrollments by student attributes (e.g., count enrollments where StdState = 'CA').
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to compute aggregated metrics (counts, sums, averages) across enrollments without explicitly aggregating at the intended grain — using it directly in aggregates risks double-counting if later joined to other one-to-many tables. | Do not use this view as if it were a pure student-level (one-row-per-student) table. Its grain is enrollment (OfferNo, StdNo); multiple enrollments per student will appear as multiple rows. | Do not use this view to infer student-level time series or cohorts without first collapsing to student-level (e.g., first enrollment or distinct StdNo) because repeated enrollments will bias cohort membership or rates. | Do not join naively to any table that is one-to-many from enrollment (for example an attendance or grade-component table) without aggregating that child table to enrollment-level first — otherwise measures tied to enrollment may be multiplied.
params.output_schema: OfferNo: enrollment offer identifier – sourced from university_enrollment.OfferNo | StdNo: student identifier for the enrollment – sourced from university_enrollment.StdNo (also the join key to university_student.StdNo) | EnrGrade: the enrollment-level grade/value for this OfferNo-StdNo pair – sourced from university_enrollment.EnrGrade | StdFirstName: student's first name – sourced from university_student.StdFirstName | StdLastName: student's last name – sourced from university_student.StdLastName | StdCity: student's city – sourced from university_student.StdCity | StdState: student's state – sourced from university_student.StdState | StdZip: student's postal code – sourced from university_student.StdZip | StdMajor: student's major – sourced from university_student.StdMajor | StdClass: student's class/year (e.g., sophomore) – sourced from university_student.StdClass | StdGPA: student's GPA – sourced from university_student.StdGPA
params.grounded_columns: university_enrollment.OfferNo | university_enrollment.StdNo | university_enrollment.EnrGrade | university_student.StdNo | university_student.StdFirstName | university_student.StdLastName | university_student.StdCity | university_student.StdState | university_student.StdZip | university_student.StdMajor | university_student.StdClass | university_student.StdGPA
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view; all output columns are direct column passthroughs. For clarity: EnrGrade = university_enrollment.EnrGrade (no aggregation), StdGPA = university_student.StdGPA (no aggregation).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: Join this view to a student-level one-row-per-student dimension on StdNo (for example, a clean student dimension that is guaranteed one-row-per-StdNo) — safe because this view is one-row-per-enrollment (OfferNo, StdNo); joining a one-row-per-student relation will not duplicate enrollment rows or their attributes. | cardinality-SAFE: Join to an offerings dimension keyed by OfferNo (one-row-per-offer) — safe because that is one-to-one with OfferNo and will not multiply rows. | NOT safe: Do NOT join this view directly to any table/view that is one-to-many from enrollment (for example, enrollment_attendance_events or grade_components) without first aggregating those child tables to OfferNo+StdNo. Joining them directly will multiply enrollment rows and therefore produce inflated counts or duplicated enrollment attributes. | NOT safe: Do NOT join this view to a raw transactions table that contains multiple transactions per StdNo if you expect student-level counts — this view remains at the enrollment grain and will produce multiple rows per student if there are multiple enrollments. | Guidance: If you need enrollment-level measures combined with many child rows (e.g., multiple payments per enrollment), aggregate the child table to OfferNo+StdNo (sum/count/avg as appropriate) before joining back to this view to preserve correct measures.
params.comparison: use offerings_with_faculty instead when you need faculty/faculty attributes for each offering — that view is focused on OfferNo-enriched with faculty and may include different join logic or columns. | use accounts_with_rep_and_region or sibling JOIN views in the hardware_* family only when working in the hardware domain; they are unrelated. This view should be used for university enrollment/student joins specifically. | If you need student-level deduplicated metrics (one row per StdNo), derive a student-level view by aggregating this view (e.g., SELECT StdNo, MAX(StdFirstName) ... FROM students_with_enrollment_and_gpa GROUP BY StdNo) or use a dedicated student dimension; do not substitute this view for that purpose.

views.name: offerings_with_faculty
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.OfferNo AS OfferNo,
  o.CourseNo AS CourseNo,
  o.OffTerm AS OffTerm,
  o.OffYear AS OffYear,
  o.OffLocation AS OffLocation,
  o.OffTime AS OffTime,
  o.FacNo AS FacNo,
  o.OffDays AS OffDays,
  f.FacFirstName AS FacFirstName,
  f.FacLastName AS FacLastName,
  f.FacCity AS FacCity,
  f.FacState AS FacState,
  f.FacDept AS FacDept,
  f.FacRank AS FacRank,
  f.FacSalary AS FacSalary
FROM university_offering AS o
LEFT JOIN university_faculty AS f ON o.FacNo = f.FacNo

params.description: Provides one row per course offering (OfferNo) enriched with the assigned faculty member's attributes (name, location, department, rank, salary).
params.when_to_use: Lookup faculty attributes for a specific offering (by OfferNo) or to display offering-level details alongside the faculty who taught/are assigned to it. | Reporting or UI rows where the natural grain is the offering (one row per OfferNo) and you want faculty metadata (name, city, state, dept, rank, salary). | Filtering/slicing offerings by faculty attributes (e.g., show offerings in 2024 taught by faculty in Dept X).
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to a student-enrollment table (one-to-many to offerings) and then aggregating without re-aggregation — doing so will double-count or multiply offering-level measures because this view is at the offering grain, not the enrollment grain. | Using it as a source for faculty-level aggregates (e.g., headcount of faculty) without first deduplicating by faculty key — multiple offerings by the same faculty will appear multiple times and will overcount faculty if simply COUNTed. | Joining to another many-to-many relationship (e.g., offering -> meeting_times or offering -> materials) directly without aggregating the many-side first — that will multiply offering rows and silently inflate counts or sums. | Using it as the basis for aggregated financial metrics that expect pre-aggregated faculty salary or cost per faculty per year — this view surfaces raw faculty salary per faculty row; summing FacSalary across offerings will overstate total salary unless offers represent disjoint salary responsibilities.
params.output_schema: OfferNo: unique identifier for the offering — derived from university_offering.OfferNo | CourseNo: course identifier for the offering — derived from university_offering.CourseNo | OffTerm: term code/label for the offering (e.g., Fall/Spring) — derived from university_offering.OffTerm | OffYear: year of the offering — derived from university_offering.OffYear | OffLocation: location/campus of the offering — derived from university_offering.OffLocation | OffTime: scheduled time for the offering — derived from university_offering.OffTime | FacNo: faculty identifier assigned to the offering — derived from university_offering.FacNo | OffDays: days of week the offering meets — derived from university_offering.OffDays | FacFirstName: faculty first name — derived from university_faculty.FacFirstName | FacLastName: faculty last name — derived from university_faculty.FacLastName | FacCity: faculty home/city — derived from university_faculty.FacCity | FacState: faculty state — derived from university_faculty.FacState | FacDept: faculty department — derived from university_faculty.FacDept | FacRank: faculty rank/title — derived from university_faculty.FacRank | FacSalary: faculty salary (presumably current or stored salary) — derived from university_faculty.FacSalary
params.grounded_columns: university_offering.OfferNo | university_offering.CourseNo | university_offering.OffTerm | university_offering.OffYear | university_offering.OffLocation | university_offering.OffTime | university_offering.FacNo | university_offering.OffDays | university_faculty.FacNo | university_faculty.FacFirstName | university_faculty.FacLastName | university_faculty.FacCity | university_faculty.FacState | university_faculty.FacDept | university_faculty.FacRank | university_faculty.FacSalary
params.metric: No aggregate metrics are defined in this view; all outputs are base columns (exact column pass-through). | FacSalary = university_faculty.FacSalary (raw salary value on the faculty table; not normalized or prorated).
params.composition: Safe to join this view to dimension tables that are one-to-one with OfferNo or one-to-one with the referenced keys, for example: |   - Join to a course-dimension keyed by CourseNo on offerings.CourseNo = course_dim.CourseNo — safe because course_dim should be one-row-per-course and will not duplicate offering rows. |   - Join to a term/calendar dimension keyed by (OffTerm, OffYear) — safe because the calendar dim is one-row-per-term. | Do NOT join this view directly to tables/views that are one-to-many from OfferNo without re-aggregation first, because that will duplicate offering rows and multiply any measures derived from this view. Examples to avoid or handle carefully: |   - Do not join directly to an enrollment or student roster table keyed by OfferNo (many students per offering) unless you aggregate the enrollment side first (e.g., count students per OfferNo) or you plan to work at the enrollment grain. |   - Do not join directly to an offering-meeting-times or offering-materials table (many meeting rows per offering) without collapsing those rows to one per OfferNo, otherwise offering rows will multiply. | If you need to compute offering-level aggregates after joining to a many-side, pre-aggregate the many-side by OfferNo and then join back to this view on OfferNo to preserve cardinality (one row per OfferNo). | Note on faculty duplication: Multiple offerings may reference the same FacNo. Joining this view to a faculty-level aggregation (one-row-per-faculty) is safe only if that faculty aggregation is deduplicated by FacNo. Conversely, using this view to compute faculty counts must deduplicate by FacNo to avoid counting the same faculty multiple times.
params.comparison: use students_with_enrollment_and_gpa JOIN instead when you need student enrollment and GPA information alongside offerings — that sibling includes enrollment grain and student-level fields which this offering-level view does not provide. | use accounts_with_rep_and_region JOIN when you need sales-rep and region enrichments for account-level reporting — it's a sibling JOIN view designed for account-level augmentation while offerings_with_faculty is offering-level and academic. | use hardware_product_master NORM or hardware_customer_master NORM for normalized master data when you need canonical product/customer attributes outside of a join — those siblings are normalized masters, whereas offerings_with_faculty is an offering-level join between offering and faculty. | use an AGG sibling (e.g., monthly_sales_by_product_year) when you require pre-aggregated metrics — offerings_with_faculty contains only raw columns and will not supply rollup metrics needed for aggregated analysis.
